learningObjective: Distinguish real benefits and limits of continuous batching from common overclaims.
stem: Select all correct statements about continuous (iteration-level) batching in LLM serving. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: Continuous batching removes head-of-line blocking under variable-length outputs: short requests exit as soon as they finish rather than waiting for the longest request in the batch.
Continuous batching reduces per-token latency (TPOT) below the batch-1 baseline because sharing weight loads across requests amortizes HBM bandwidth per token.
Continuous batching is only meaningful for MoE models; dense transformers see no benefit because their batch dynamics are fully static.

Continuous batching improves aggregate throughput but does not improve (and may slightly worsen) per-token latency for a single request compared to running that request alone: joining a batch adds interference.

explanation: A is correct: iteration-level batching's canonical benefit is removing HoL blocking. D is correct: continuous batching improves throughput and fairness but a solo request on a dedicated GPU actually has the fastest TPOT for that request; joining a shared batch adds contention. B is wrong: continuous batching does share weight loads across requests (which raises throughput), but TPOT for a single request is bounded below by the total per-token bandwidth cost — joining a batch does not shorten one request's own per-token latency. C is wrong: dense transformers benefit primarily.

optionExplanations.D: Correct: throughput up, per-request TPOT slightly up.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: TPOT is per-request; batching cross-shares weights but does not reduce one request's per-step cost.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: dense models are the primary beneficiaries.

nonImplications: Does not imply continuous batching solves all throughput problems.
Does not imply continuous batching is beneficial with only one active request.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses throughput improvement with per-request latency reduction.
